home.title: Questions about rtylr
home.intro: Quick answers to what people ask first.

items.question: What is rtylr?
items.answer: rtylr is one workspace for running a business. Work, finance, customers, team, operations and sales share the same records, so an update in one place shows up everywhere else. Caret, the AI built into rtylr, can answer questions and get things done across all of it.

items.question: How much does rtylr cost?
items.answer: rtylr has not published its prices yet. The Free plan is genuinely free, needs no card, and covers 10 team members at one location with the core rtylr suite, so you can run a location on it today. Pro and Scale are quoted: tell us your team size and how many locations you run. See rtylr.com/pricing for what each plan includes.

items.question: What is Caret?
items.answer: Caret is the AI assistant built into rtylr. Ask it about your business, like which invoices are overdue or how sales did this week, and it can act on the answer, like sending reminders or drafting an invoice. It also works as an everyday assistant for writing, research and questions about anything else.

items.question: Is my data mine?
items.answer: Yes. Every rtylr account exports clean CSVs of customers, orders, staff, invoices and inventory at any time from the settings page, with no support ticket. Data lives in the EU or US region, your choice. See rtylr.com/trust for compliance detail and rtylr.com/legal/security for the security architecture.

items.question: How much does rtylr cost?
items.answer: rtylr has not published its prices yet. The Free plan is genuinely free and needs no card, so you can run a location on it today. For Pro or Scale, contact us and we will talk through your team size and locations. We would rather quote you honestly than put a number here we might change.

items.question: Can I switch plans at any time?
items.answer: Yes. Upgrade and the new features unlock instantly. Downgrade and the change applies at the end of the current period. Your data, team, and settings stay put.

items.question: Is there a free trial for Pro?
items.answer: Every new workspace starts with a 14-day Pro trial, and it needs no card. At day 14 it reverts to the Free plan automatically unless you tell us otherwise.

items.question: What happens when I hit 10 seats on Free?
items.answer: You're prompted to move to Pro before adding seat 11. Nothing breaks. Your data, reports, and configurations all carry over.

items.question: When does Scale apply?
items.answer: Scale is built for teams past 30 active seats. It removes the seat and location limits and adds SSO, audit logs, a dedicated success manager and an SLA.

items.question: Any contract or lock-in?
items.answer: None. You can cancel at any time, and your data is exportable while the account is open.

items.question: What should I prepare for the demo?
items.answer: Nothing is required. If you would rather see your own data than a sample, bring a menu or a SKU list, a recent invoice, and a rough idea of how many people and how many locations you run. Those are enough to show the register, stock, payroll and the books working against something you recognise.

items.question: Is the demo a sales call?
items.answer: It is a 30 minute product walkthrough, run by someone who built rtylr. You do not need one in order to start: the Free plan covers 10 team members at one location and needs no card, so you can sign up and look around on your own first. The walkthrough is for the questions a signup page cannot answer.

workspace.title: Questions about the workspace
workspace.intro: How the parts fit together, and what they handle.

items.question: Can I use only part of the workspace?
items.answer: Yes. Start with the area that matters most to your business and add the rest when you need it. Everything stays in one workspace on the same records, with no separate logins or exports.

items.question: What can the workspace do that separate tools cannot?
items.answer: Assign a task to a staff member who already exists in HR, attach it to a customer who already exists in CRM, and push billable hours onto an invoice in Finance, without copying anything between tools. The tasks, boards, comments and automations you would expect are all there; the connection to real business records is the part a separate tracker cannot have.

items.question: Does checkout work offline?
items.answer: Yes. rtylr POS keeps a full local copy of the menu, modifiers and active orders. When the internet drops, the register keeps taking orders, printing tickets and processing cash. Card transactions queue and settle automatically once the connection returns, so a Saturday night outage does not stop the floor.

items.question: Does it support multiple currencies?
items.answer: Yes. Invoice in any currency, and rtylr converts using the exchange rate at invoice time. P&L reports can be read in any reporting currency, with FX lines shown explicitly rather than folded into the totals.

items.question: Does it handle multiple locations?
items.answer: Yes. Every item can be stocked at multiple locations with per-location counts, reorder thresholds and transfer tracking. A purchase order can be split across warehouses, and staff see only their assigned location by default.

plans-billing.p1: rtylr is offered on a Free plan and paid plans (Pro, Scale). Plan features, limits, and prices are described at <pricingLink>rtylr.com/pricing</pricingLink>. By subscribing to a paid plan, you authorize us (or our payment processor) to charge the payment method on file for recurring fees, taxes, and any overages defined on the pricing page.
plans-billing.p2: Unless otherwise stated, all fees are exclusive of applicable taxes. We use Paddle Inc. as the Merchant of Record for most transactions; Paddle’s payment terms may also apply to your purchase.

seat-proration.p1: Paid plans are billed per active seat. A “seat” is any user with login access to your workspace. Seats are billed on a daily-proration basis:
list1: When you add a seat mid-cycle, you are charged only for the days remaining in that billing period.
When you remove a seat mid-cycle, the remaining days of that seat are credited against your next invoice.
Billing is summarised at the end of each period so you can see exactly which seats were active on which days.
seat-proration.p2: On the Scale plan, tiered pricing applies automatically when your workspace exceeds 30 active seats during the billing period.

trial-refunds.p1: New workspaces may start on a trial of a paid plan. At trial end, the workspace automatically reverts to the Free plan unless a payment method is added. You may cancel at any time; cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period.
trial-refunds.p2: Because rtylr is offered on a daily-prorated basis, unused days within the current cycle are credited forward rather than refunded. We will issue a refund only where required by applicable consumer-protection law.

meta.title: rtylr Privacy Policy: How Voxire Handles Your Data | rtylr
meta.description: How rtylr and Voxire handle your personal data, under GDPR, CCPA, and equivalent laws: what we collect, who we share it with, retention and your rights.
meta.schemaDescription: How rtylr and Voxire handle your personal data.

overview.p1: This Privacy Policy describes how Voxire (“we”) collects, uses, shares, and protects personal data in connection with the rtylr platform. We act as a data controller for personal data about our customers and website visitors, and as a data processor for Customer Data that our customers process in rtylr on behalf of their own end-users.
overview.p2: If you are an end-user of a business that uses rtylr (for example, a diner whose email is captured in a restaurant’s CRM), the rtylr customer is the controller of your data. Please contact that business first to exercise your rights; we will help them do so.

subsections.heading: Account and billing data
subsections.body: When you create a workspace we collect name, email, business name, role, country, and a password hash. When you subscribe, our payment processor (Paddle) collects billing address, tax identifiers, and card tokens. We do not store raw card numbers on our servers.

subsections.heading: Customer Data
subsections.body: Depending on the applications your business uses, Customer Data can include customer contact and loyalty records, orders, employee and payroll records, recruitment applications and CVs, invoices, schedules, and tasks. The business determines why this data is collected and supplies its own notices and lawful basis. A privacy-policy acknowledgement is not consent to unrelated marketing.

subsections.heading: Usage and device data
subsections.body: We log IP address, browser/device type, referring URL, pages accessed, and timestamps. We use this to operate, secure, and improve rtylr, and to generate aggregate analytics.

subsections.heading: Cookies and similar technologies
subsections.body: See the <cookiesAnchor>Cookies</cookiesAnchor> section below for details.

list1: provide, secure, and maintain the Service;
process billing and send transactional emails;
respond to support requests and improve product quality;
detect and prevent fraud, abuse, and security incidents;
send product announcements to the primary owner on a workspace (you can opt out from your profile);
comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms.

legal-bases.p1: For EEA/UK residents, we rely on the following legal bases:
list1: Contract, to provide the Service and manage billing.
Legitimate interests, to secure the Service, detect abuse, and improve features. We balance these interests against your rights.
Consent, for non-essential cookies and certain marketing communications. You can withdraw consent at any time.
Legal obligation, when we are required to retain or disclose data by law.

sharing.p1: We use service providers and other recipients to operate rtylr. Their legal role depends on the service: a payment merchant may act as an independent controller rather than a subprocessor. The providers named in this notice include:
list1: Cloudflare, CDN, DNS, DDoS protection.
Paddle, payment processing and merchant of record.
Firebase / Google Cloud, authentication infrastructure.
Resend / Postmark, transactional email delivery.
PostHog / Axiom, product analytics and error tracking (when enabled).
Google Analytics, optional website analytics after acceptance; Sentry, application diagnostics when configured.
sharing.p2: A current list is available on request at <privacyMail>privacy@voxire.com</privacyMail>. We notify customers before adding a new sub-processor that has access to Customer Data.
sharing.p3: We do not sell personal data. We do not share personal data with advertisers.

international.p1: rtylr may process data outside your country of residence. Where we transfer data from the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, we rely on the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) or an equivalent mechanism.

list1: Account data is retained for the life of the account plus 30 days for recovery, then deleted within 60 days.
Billing records are retained for 7 years to comply with tax and accounting rules.
Security logs are retained for 90 days; audit logs for 12 months.
Encrypted backups are on a rolling schedule and purged within 90 days.

your-rights.p1: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:
list1: access the personal data we hold about you;
correct inaccurate data;
request deletion of your data;
object to or restrict processing;
port your data to another service;
withdraw consent at any time (where processing relies on consent);
lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
your-rights.p2: To exercise your rights, email <privacyMail>privacy@voxire.com</privacyMail>. We may request information reasonably necessary to verify your identity or an authorized representative. We respond within the period required by applicable law and explain any permitted extension or refusal. You may complain to your local data-protection authority and, where applicable, appeal a refusal. We will not discriminate against you for exercising your rights.

cookies.p1: We use three categories of cookies:
list1: Strictly necessary, authentication, load balancing, CSRF protection. These are always on.
Preference, remember your language, theme, and workspace selection.
Analytics, help us understand which pages work and which don’t. These only run with your consent (visible on first visit).
cookies.p2: Use “Cookie preferences” in the website footer to reopen your choice and withdraw optional analytics consent. The rtylr-consent cookie remembers your choice for up to one year across rtylr.com subdomains. You can also remove cookies in your browser; removing authentication cookies may sign you out.

children.p1: rtylr is not directed to children under 16. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If you believe a child has registered, contact <privacyMail>privacy@voxire.com</privacyMail> and we will delete the account.

changes.p1: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes to the Service or the law. When we do, we update the “Last updated” date and, for material changes, notify primary owners by email.

contact.p1: Our Data Protection contact is reachable at <privacyMail>privacy@voxire.com</privacyMail>. Postal mail: Voxire, c/o Data Protection, Beirut, Lebanon.

contactStrip.title: Data request, complaint, or just a question?
contactStrip.body: Email <privacyMail>privacy@voxire.com</privacyMail> with your request. Please identify the relevant account or business without sending passwords, payment-card details, or unnecessary sensitive documents.

meta.title: Security at rtylr: Reporting and Assurance | rtylr
meta.description: Security reporting, data-processing considerations, and assurance information for rtylr, with monitoring and incident response and how to disclose a flaw.
meta.schemaDescription: Security reporting, data-processing considerations, and assurance information for rtylr.

program.p1: This page describes security considerations for rtylr. Controls depend on the service, deployment, and configuration. Contact <secMail>security@voxire.com</secMail> for current evidence and contractual commitments before relying on a particular control.

monitoring.p1: Report suspected incidents to <secMail>security@voxire.com</secMail>. Where we act as a processor, applicable data-protection law can require notice to the customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal-data breach. Regulatory and individual notifications depend on the facts and applicable law; a 72-hour regulatory deadline is not a general waiting period for notifying customers.

list1: Data protection. Applicable duties depend on the processing and jurisdictions involved. Ask for the applicable data-processing terms and transfer arrangements before sending personal data.
Payment security. Subscription payments use a payment provider. Outsourcing payments does not by itself establish PCI DSS compliance for rtylr, a merchant, or a POS deployment.

Independent assurance. This page does not establish ISO 27001 certification or a completed SOC 2 examination. Request a current report, its scope, and covered period before relying on an assurance claim.

disclosure.p1: We welcome reports from security researchers. If you believe you’ve found a vulnerability, please email <secMail>security@voxire.com</secMail> with:
list1: a clear description of the issue and its impact;
steps to reproduce;
a minimal proof of concept using only accounts and data you own or are expressly authorized to test. Do not access, copy, modify, or disclose other people’s data; stop and report if you encounter it.
disclosure.p2: We commit to acknowledging receipt within 48 hours, working in good faith on a fix, and crediting you publicly once the issue is resolved (unless you prefer to remain anonymous). We do not take legal action against researchers acting in good faith under this policy.

contact.p1: For security questions, reports, or compliance requests, email <secMail>security@voxire.com</secMail>. For urgent issues, WhatsApp +961 3 849 744.

contactStrip.title: Need security or data-processing information?
contactStrip.body: Email <secMail>security@voxire.com</secMail> to request current documentation and confirm what is available for your deployment.

meta.title: The rtylr workspace · Work, finance, customers, team and more
meta.description: One workspace for running a business: projects, finance, customers, team, operations, sales and insights on the same records, with Caret, the AI built in.
meta.schemaDescription: The rtylr workspace brings work, finance, customers, team, operations, sales and insights together on shared records, so an update in one place reaches the rest.

hero.title:
Every part of your business.
One workspace.
hero.subtitle: Work, finance, customers, team, operations, sales and insights share the same records, so nothing gets typed twice and nothing falls between tools.

work.label: Work
work.title:
Projects and tasks.
Linked to the real work.
work.body: Boards, lists, timelines and calendars for every team, all on the same data underneath.

features.title: Views for every team.
features.body: Board, list, timeline or calendar. Each team picks its view; the data stays the same.

features.title: Tasks that link to reality.
features.body: Attach a task to a customer, a supplier, an invoice or a shift. When it moves, everything updates.

features.title: Automations built in.
features.body: When a purchase order is approved, a task lands on purchasing. When payroll closes, HR gets a reminder.

finance.label: Finance
finance.title:
Money, handled.
The books keep up on their own.
finance.body: Invoices, expenses, tax and a live P&L, fed by everything else in the workspace.

features.title: Invoices that collect themselves.
features.body: Recurring schedules, automatic reminders and one-click payment. Paid invoices reconcile against the books.

features.title: Expenses captured at source.
features.body: Snap the receipt, categorise it by policy, and take it from approved to paid in the same place.

features.title: A live P&L.
features.body: Every sale, invoice and payroll run rolls into the profit-and-loss as it happens, not at month-end.

features.title: Tax without the scramble.
features.body: Jurisdiction-aware sales tax, quarter-end snapshots and one export for your accountant.

customers.label: Customers
customers.title:
Every customer.
Remembered.
customers.body: Profiles, segments, loyalty and campaigns, updated by every sale and conversation.

features.title: Segments that make sense.
features.body: Slice by visit frequency, average spend or last order, save it, and send a campaign.

features.title: Loyalty built in.
features.body: Points, tiers and rewards, applied automatically at checkout.

features.title: Messages that read personal.
features.body: Email and SMS templates with personalisation, sent on triggers like a birthday, a lapse or a first visit.

team.label: Team
team.title:
Your people.
Looked after.
team.body: Schedules, time, payroll and time off in one place, with permissions for who sees what.

features.title: Schedules that publish themselves.
features.body: Drag, drop, publish. People are notified the moment a shift posts, and conflicts are caught first.

features.title: Time and attendance.
features.body: Clock in with a PIN or a geofence, with rounding and break rules built in.

features.title: Payroll from real hours.
features.body: Hours, tips, deductions and taxes roll up automatically, with pay stubs for everyone.

features.title: Time off, clearly.
features.body: Requests, approvals and balances in one place.

operations.label: Operations
operations.title:
Stock that counts itself.
Suppliers that stay in sync.
operations.body: Inventory, purchasing and transfers that move as you sell.

features.title: Every item, every variant.
features.body: Real-time counts as sales happen, down to the component.

features.title: Suppliers and purchase orders.
features.body: Reorder at a threshold, compare supplier prices and track arrivals line by line.

features.title: Multi-location transfers.
features.body: Move stock between sites with a full audit trail.

features.title: Low-stock alerts.
features.body: Thresholds based on how fast things sell, routed to the right person.

sales.label: Sales
sales.title:
Checkout that keeps up.
And feeds everything else.
sales.body: A point of sale that updates stock, revenue and the customer the moment a sale goes through.

features.title: Every payment method.
features.body: Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, cash, gift cards and house accounts on one register.

features.title: Splits, tabs and tips.
features.body: Split by item or seat, run tabs, and send tips straight to payroll.

features.title: Works offline.
features.body: Sales queue locally when the internet drops and sync the moment it's back.

insights.label: Insights
insights.title:
The numbers.
Always current.
insights.body: Revenue, customers and margins across the whole workspace, with Caret on hand to explain what changed.

features.title: One view of the business.
features.body: Sales, costs, people and customers side by side, without exporting anything.

features.title: Ask instead of digging.
features.body: Ask Caret why a number moved and get an answer from your own records.

features.title: Live, not nightly.
features.body: Numbers update as the business runs, not after an overnight sync.
